abandon: The mechanism says T 0.6's better finished-answer accuracy comes from removing tail draws at early plan decisions (forks), so cooling only the first ~1,000 tokens should keep that gain without loops. Two board items already contradict the cause it names. (1) result-34897a cooled exactly the fork positions over the whole answer and got no finished-answer gain: 'T 1.0 with T 0.6 where entropy > 0.9 nats (mean of 2 samples 403.5)' with 'Cap hits per 500: T 1.0 22.5, forks only 33, confident only 44, both (T 0.6) 98'. That is 403.5 right of 467 finished (86.4 %) against plain T 1.0's 410.5 of 477.5 (86.0 %). The ten extra cap hits should, if anything, have raised that ratio by selection. Cooling confident positions instead gives 403.5 of 456 (88.5 %). So what rise there is in finished accuracy follows cooling at confident (slip) positions, not at forks where plans are chosen. An early-only window covers a subset of those same forks, so it cannot recover a gain that cooling all forks did not produce. (2) result-faf15a finds that the base's located wrong steps are more probable than their own control text, not tail draws: 'Under the base the wrong step has log-prob -0.53 per token vs -0.63 for control text (W4 refuted): truncation or low temperature cannot remove these steps'. For wrong plans in particular RL does not lower them either ('wrong plan +0.03'). The '94 % vs about 90 %' contrast the mechanism starts from (knowledge-13cff3: 'on the 402 problems that finish at T 0.6, T 1.0 gets 361-364 against 378') conditions on the T 0.6 sample itself finishing. A wrong T 0.6 line tends to loop and drop out, so the contrast is at least partly selection, not evidence of better early decisions. That is the reading items (1) and (2) support.
